To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The clinical and autoptic diagnosis of the cause of death are not always concordant.

(1) the prevalence of clinical and autoptic diagnosis discrepancies in Italy is 10%; (2) the prevalence of discrepancies is 20% in the elderly (over 80 years of age); (3) the prevalence of autoptic diagnosis discrepancies is 10% in the young (under 40 years of age); and (4) the prevalence of diagnosis discrepancies in the young is 20% if death is caused by an accident or suicide.
The number of discrepancies between the clinical and autoptic diagnosis in Italy is 7.5% (6.7% of the cases in 1990-1999, 9.1% in 2000-2009).
